items.description: 给国产电视的一块干净桌面：参照 tvOS 设计的开源 Android TV 桌面，没有广告，开机自动接管。A tvOS-style launcher for Xiaomi, TCL and other China-market TVs.
items.readme:
# Aerial **给国产电视的一块干净桌面。** 参照 Apple TV 做的 Android TV 桌面：没有广告，没有推荐流，只有你的 App、壁纸和航拍屏保。
适合小米、TCL、创维、索尼等国产电视，也能装在盒子和投影仪上。开机自动进入，待机也不会被清理。 **中文** · [English](README.en.md) ![Aerial 首页](site/img/home.jpg) | 电视自带的桌面 | 换上 Aerial 之后 | |:---:|:---:| | | |
## 功能

- **首页**：常用的一排 App 放在屏幕下方的玻璃底板上，往下是全部 App。小米「应用中心」「米家」这类藏起来的系统 App 也在。 - **整理**：长按 OK 键（或按菜单键）可以移动、放进文件夹、隐藏、卸载。固定到主屏幕的 HDMI 可以选接的是 Apple TV、PlayStation、Switch、Xbox、电脑等，换成对应的图标，也能在手机上起名字。 - **用手机整理**：扫电视上的二维码，手机上就是和电视一样的图标网格：按住拖动排序，点一下改名、换图标、放进文件夹或隐藏，也能把 HDMI 等信号源加到主屏幕。 - **控制中心**：在第一排按上键到右上角打开，有信号源、网络、设置、音量、亮度和个性化。 - **屏保**：Apple TV 的 114 段航拍影片，电视支持时播 4K 或 4K 杜比视界，也可以换成照片、时钟或从手机添加的本地视频（[说明](docs/SCREENSAVER_VIDEOS.md)）。 - **壁纸**：必应每日精选、14 张内置壁纸、用手机扫码传的照片，或者航拍：停在主屏幕 10 秒后在磁贴后面播放，按任意键停在当前画面。 - **个性化**：单排或双排、时钟大小和位置、App 名称、焦点样式、按键声音，都能改。

## 安装 不用 root，不动系统应用，随时能还原。电脑和电视连同一个网络。 ### 1. 打开电视的 ADB 调试 | 电视 | 怎么打开 | |---|---| | **小米 / Redmi** | 设置 → 关于 → 连续按「产品型号」进入开发者模式，再到 设置 → 账号与安全，打开「ADB 调试」和「安装未知来源的应用」 | | **TCL / 雷鸟** | 设置 → 关于 → 本机信息，快速按遥控器「上下左右」，在底部的「更多」里打开 ADB | | **海尔 / 模卡** | 按电视机身上的信号源键，再用遥控器按「左左上右」，在工厂菜单里打开「ADB 调试开关」，别动其他选项 | | **OPPO（含 S1）** | 设置 → 系统 → 关于本机 → 设备型号，按「上上右右」再按确认；再到 设置 → 系统 → 开发者选项，打开「USB 调试」。IP 在 设置 → 网络 → 已连接的网络 最下面 | | **其他 Android TV** | 设置 → 设备偏好设置 → 关于 → 连按「内部版本号」7 次，再在开发者选项里打开「USB 调试」 | 电视的 IP 在「设置 → 网络 → 已连接的网络」里。第一次连接时，电视会问是否允许调试，选「始终允许」。 更细的分品牌说明（包括打不开 ADB 的机型）见 [docs/devices/adb-by-brand.md](docs/devices/adb-by-brand.md)。 ### 2. 安装 **让 Agent 装（推荐）**：把下面这段发给能在电脑上运行命令的 Agent（WorkBuddy、豆包电脑版、千问电脑版、Trae、Claude Code、Codex 等）： ```text 请帮我把开源电视桌面 Aerial 装到我的电视上，并设为开机进入的桌面。 电视 IP：<电视IP> 保持 ADB 常开：要 安装说明在这里：https://aerial.qust.me/agent.md （打不开时用 https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pengchujin/aerial-tv/main/site/agent.md ） 请先完整读完安装说明再动手，然后在我的电脑上亲自运行命令，不要只把步骤告诉我。需要我在电视上操作时提醒我。 最后按说明里的「验收」，把这几条命令的原始输出原样贴给我： - adb shell "cmd package resolve-activity --brief -a android.intent.action.MAIN -c android.intent.category.HOME" - adb shell settings get secure enabled_accessibility_services - 按主页键后的 adb shell "dumpsys window | grep mCurrentFocus" ``` 手机上的豆包、网页版聊天只会把步骤告诉你，不会执行；要用能跑命令的电脑版 / 工作版（豆包电脑版或豆包工作版、WorkBuddy、千问电脑版、Trae、Claude Code、Codex 等）。Agent 说装好了，看它贴出的 `mCurrentFocus` 输出里有没有 `app.orchard.tv`。 **没有电脑**：有用户用手机上的甲壳虫 ADB 助手、超级小爱装成功过，本仓库没有逐一实测。步骤和上面的 Windows 步骤一样，装好后建议再用电脑跑一遍验收。 **一行命令（macOS / Linux）**： ```bash curl -fsSL https://aerial.qust.me/install.sh | KEEP_ADB=1 TV=192.168.1.20 bash ``` **手动**：下载 [aerial-standard.apk](https://aerial.qust.me/download/aerial-standard.apk)，然后： ```bash adb connect 192.168.1.20:5555 adb install -r aerial-standard.apk adb shell pm grant app.orchard.tv android.permission.WRITE_SECURE_SETTINGS adb shell cmd notification allow_listener app.orchard.tv/app.orchard.tv.guard.RevivalListener adb shell appops set app.orchard.tv SYSTEM_ALERT_WINDOW allow adb shell am start -n app.orchard.tv/.MainActivity ``` Windows 用 Agent 装，或照[安装说明](site/agent.md)里的 Windows 步骤。 **升级**：1.32 起，有新版本时控制中心会出现「有新版本」，点进去选「下载并安装」，在电视自己的安装界面确认（小米、TCL 上验证过），装完回到 Aerial，设置都保留。电视不让 App 安装应用时，升级就是再运行一次安装命令：升级页上有二维码，手机扫码能直接复制这台电视的命令，或者交给 Agent。1.31 及以前没有这个按钮，这一次还是要再运行一次安装命令。 ### 还原 ```bash curl -fsSL https://aerial.qust.me/install.sh | TV=192.168.1.20 bash -s restore ``` 最后加 `--uninstall`（`bash -s restore --uninstall`）会顺便卸载 Aerial。不能运行 bash（Windows）时，逐条的 adb 命令见[安装说明的「还原」](site/agent.md#还原)。 想交给 AI 还原，把这段直接发过去（要能在电脑上运行命令）： ```text 请按 https://aerial.qust.me/agent.md 里「还原」一节的步骤，把我电视（IP：<电视IP>）的桌面还原成原来的，Aerial 先不卸载。 请在我的电脑上亲自运行命令，最后把 settings get secure enabled_accessibility_services 和按主页键后的 dumpsys window | grep mCurrentFocus 原始输出贴给我。 ``` ### 常见问题 - **我的电视能用吗**：见下面的[支持的机型](#支持的机型)。 - **只用 U 盘装了 APK**：1.32 起「我的应用」里有 Aerial 的图标，打开后会提示怎么设为主屏幕。只装 APK 时按主页键、开机和待机后还是原桌面，要用上面的命令或 Agent 再设置一次（会覆盖安装，不丢设置）。 - **TCL 弹出「多屏互动」**：按遥控器「右」再按确认，选「同意」。 - **创维 `adb install` 报 `INSTALL_FAILED_USER_RESTRICTED`**：先运行 `adb shell settings put global verifier_verify_adb_installs 0` 再装（用户反馈，详见[安装说明](site/agent.md#常见情况)）。 - **提示不允许安装桌面类 App**：命令最后加 `-s guard`，或下载 [aerial-guard.apk](https://aerial.qust.me/download/aerial-guard.apk)。 - **`KEEP_ADB=1` 是什么**：小米待机后会关掉 ADB，加上它 Aerial 会重新打开，方便以后升级。 - **原来的桌面、会员、小爱、账号和有线电视还在吗**：都在。Aerial 只换桌面，原来的桌面在 App 列表里（小米影视、PatchWall 从「桌面」磁贴进），小爱同学、小米账号、有线电视照常。开机广告是固件播的，去不掉。 ## 它怎么接管桌面 国产电视大多只认自家桌面，待机时还会清理第三方 App。所以 Aerial 用一个无障碍服务，原桌面一出现就切回来（只看哪个窗口在前台，不读屏幕内容）；被清理后再靠通知监听让系统把它拉起来（不读通知）。老小米（Android 6）的桌面不报告窗口变化，守护改看系统的用量统计；有些酷开、创维固件不按标准方式启动桌面，守护也认得它们自己的桌面。原生 Android TV 上不需要这些，直接设成默认桌面就行。 ## 支持的机型 ✅ 能用　⚠️ 能用，有限制　❌ 暂时接管不了。大多来自用户反馈，带「笔记」的有详细记录。 | 品牌 | 机型 | 系统 | 情况 | |---|---|---|---| | 小米 / Redmi | MiTV-MFTR0（Redmi X65 2026）、MFFU0、MTSU0（S65 Mini LED 2026 至尊版） | Android 14 | ✅ 日常使用（[MFTR0](docs/devices/xiaomi-mitv-mftr0.md)、[MFFU0](docs/devices/xiaomi-mitv-mffu0.md)、[MTSU0](docs/devices/xiaomi-mitv-mtsu0.md)） | | 小米 | MiTV-ASTP0、NSOP0、MFTP0 | Android 9 | ✅ MFTP0 被系统清理后约 30–60 秒才回来（[笔记](docs/devices/xiaomi-mitv-mftp0.md)） | | 小米 | 小米电视 4 / 4A / 4X / 3S、小米盒子 4 | Android 6 | ✅ 1.43 起；按主页键后几秒才回到 Aerial（[笔记](docs/devices/xiaomi-android6.md)） | | 小米（峰米） | Ultraman 系列投影仪 | Android 9 | ✅（[笔记](docs/devices/xiaomi-ultraman-projector.md)） | | TCL | MT5879 国行 | Android 11 | ✅ 日常使用（[笔记](docs/devices/tcl-mt5879-cn.md)） | | TCL | 75V2（m7221） | Android 8 | ✅ 免 root，开机直达（[笔记](docs/devices/tcl-m7221-cn.md)） | | 雷鸟 | 55S595C Ultra、鹤 6 2025 Ultra | Android 11+ | ❌ 能装，接管不了主页键（[笔记](docs/devices/tcl-mt9655-cn.md)） | | 索尼 | A80J 国行、BRAVIA VH1 | Android 10 / 12 | ✅ | | 创维 / 酷开 | K3 Pro、75A7D | Android 11 | ✅ 75A7D 的信号源 1.45 起能用 | | 创维 / 酷开 | 65G60、8R134 / 8R145、aigc 系（C10 投影、P60、7T863） | Android 8–11 | ⚠️ 开机先进酷开桌面，或被系统清理后要等 20–30 秒（[笔记](docs/devices/skyworth-coocaa.md)） | | 创维 | 7T641、75A6E | Android 13 | ❌ 黑屏或卡死 | | 松下 | TH-55HX560C（创维代工） | Android 8 | ⚠️ 信号源列不出来 | | 康佳 | KKTV U86V9、2861 | Android 9 | ✅ U86V9 亮度调不了（[笔记](docs/devices/konka-kktv-u86v9.md)） | | 海信 / Vidda | VIDAA 各型号 | Android 5–14 | ⚠️ 主页键能接管，开机多数先进聚好看；VIDAA C1 投影接管不了（[笔记](docs/devices/hisense-vidaa.md)） | | OPPO | K9 | Android 9 | ⚠️ 要改包名才能装（[笔记](docs/devices/oppo-coloros-tv.md)） | | 极米 | Z7X、m7642 | Android 9 | ✅ Z7X 要用第三方工具打开 ADB（[笔记](docs/devices/xgimi-z7x.md)） | | 大眼橙 | X7 投影仪 | Android 9 | ✅ HDMI 里按主页键可以回到 Apple TV 主屏幕（[笔记](docs/devices/obe-x7.md)） | | 腾讯极光盒子 | 6 / 6SE / 7S | Android 10 / 14 | ✅ 6 正常；⚠️ 7S 开机停在原桌面（[笔记](docs/devices/tencent-aurora-box.md)） | | 其他盒子 | CM311-1（改版 ATV）、PPTV K55U27 | Android 9 | ✅ | - **不支持**：LG webOS、三星 Tizen、华为鸿蒙智慧屏，以及 Android 4.4 及更老的系统。 - **打不开 ADB**：极米 H3、老乐视、荣耀智慧屏、老康佳（看不到版本号）。 - **老电视或内存小的电视会卡**：1.48 起自动改用「流畅」效果（面板用纯色、去掉高光），也可以在 个性化 → 效果 里手动选。 你的电视能用，或者有问题，欢迎用[机型适配模板](https://github.com/pengchujin/aerial-tv/issues/new?template=device.yml)告诉我们，附上诊断信息：电脑上运行 `curl -fsSL https://aerial.qust.me/tools/report.sh | TV=<电视IP> bash`（只读，不改电视），或者在手机配置页「更多 → 反馈问题」里复制。诊断信息不含账号、IP、Wi-Fi 名称和 App 列表。 ## 开发 需要 JDK 17、Android SDK 36。 ```bash ./gradlew assembleStandardRelease assembleGuardRelease BUILD=1 KEEP_ADB=1 TV=<电视IP> tools/install.sh ``` 代码结构见 [ARCHITECTURE.md](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md)，现状和规则见 [HANDOFF.md](docs/HANDOFF.md)，各机型笔记在 [docs/devices/](docs/devices/)。 ## 许可 [MIT](LICENSE)。Inter 字体使用 [SIL Open Font License](FONT-LICENSE-OFL.txt)。天气用的国内城市表来自 [GeoNames](https://www.geonames.org)（CC BY 4.0），天气数据来自 [Open-Meteo](https://open-meteo.com)。 Aerial 是独立的开源项目，与 Apple、小米、TCL 等公司无关。航拍影片版权归 Apple，由 Apple 的服务器直接播放；每日精选图片来自必应。

items.description: GPU tensor unlock source for RTX 4090 and experimental RTX 4070 Ti SUPER; firmware generated locally
items.readme:
# GPU unlock 1.1.1 — RTX 4090 and experimental Ada GPUs

New to this project? Start with the [copy-paste Quick Start](QUICKSTART.md).

This Linux kernel module enables the SM speed-select override before the stock
NVIDIA driver starts. RTX 4090 (`10de:2684`, AD102) support has demonstrated
approximately **2× FP16 and BF16 tensor throughput with FP32 accumulation**:

| Mode | Before | After |
|---|---:|---:|
| FP16 → FP32 accumulate | 165.6 TF/s | 331.6 TF/s |
| BF16 → FP32 accumulate | 165.5 TF/s | 330.6 TF/s |

The override survived PCIe Function Level Reset (FLR), stock NVIDIA `615.78.08`
initialization and CUDA benchmarks. INT8, `dp4a` and scalar FP32 stayed near their
baseline rates. The original transaction preceded the repository cleanup; see
the [technical report](rtx4090-register-report.md) and
[original evidence](docs/evidence/rtx4090/README.md).

An independent owner run of revision `8855e7b` also completed the RTX 4090
transaction and NVIDIA driver handoff on Linux `7.2.11-arch1-1`. Matched
stock/unlocked measurements with NVIDIA `615.78.08` and the same 450 W cap
found FP16/FP32 instruction throughput **160.4 → 320.4 TF/s** and BF16/FP32
**159.7 → 320.2 TF/s**. All exercised numerical checks passed. Real cuBLAS
GEMM median throughput varied by shape: FP16 gained 12–34%, BF16 gained
16–20% at two shapes and was essentially unchanged at 4096³. These are one
matched run pair with the desktop active, not whole-application speedups or
an extended stability test. See the [matched evidence and limits](docs/evidence/rtx4090-pr1-matched/README.md)
and [testing workflow](docs/testing.md).

A modified 48 GB RTX 4090 (`10de:2684`, AD102) on Ubuntu 26.04 with Linux
`7.0.0-38-generic` and NVIDIA `610.57.04` open kernel modules also completed the
transaction and driver handoff on 2026-10-25: `fmla32` went from `1` to `0`,
FP16/FP32 instruction throughput **164.9 → 328.9 TF/s**, BF16/FP32
**164.8 → 328.7 TF/s**, with INT8, `dp4a` and scalar unchanged and no Xid. A
quantized mixture-of-experts serving workload on the same card showed **no**
gain (8K prefill 0.983×), which is consistent with quantized matmuls not
consuming the FP32-accumulate tensor path. That is one card, one cold boot and
one workload. See the [modified-card evidence and limits](docs/evidence/rtx4090-48g-modded/README.md).
Further matched owner reproductions used NVIDIA [610.57.04](docs/evidence/rtx4090-610.57.04/README.md)
and [595.91.07](docs/evidence/rtx4090-595.91.07/README.md).

A separate cold test of the Ada port on one RTX 4070 Ti SUPER
(`10de:2705`) with NVIDIA `580.178.04` measured FP16/FP32 tensor issue rate
at **95.0 → 189.9 TF/s** and BF16/FP32 at **95.0 → 189.7 TF/s** under the
same 240 W power cap. INT8 stayed at 379.5 TOP/s. The stock driver loaded,
the NVIDIA RM getter reported full FMLA32 rate, deterministic FP16/BF16 GEMM
outputs matched exactly, and owner mining recovered with fresh accepted shares.
A second matched instruction benchmark found **TF32/FP32 47.49 → 94.51 TF/s**
(1.99×), with its FP16/FP32 control also near 2×. Unsigned INT4/INT32 stayed
at approximately **754.8 TOP/s** in both states. These are register-resident
issue rates, not application GEMM or inference speedups.
A matched, verified E4M3 FP8/FP32 CUTLASS GEMM measured **59.326 TF/s stock →
59.495 TF/s unlocked** on this card, a 0.3% difference. That kernel reaches only
about 17% of this card's FP8 peak, so it cannot resolve an issue-rate change.
Other measurements do put FP8 in the affected group: an 8192³ E4M3 GEMM on a
Windows RTX 4080 SUPER measured **199.4 → 310.4 TF/s (+55.7%)** and
**199.4 → 298.7 TF/s (+49.8%)** in two runs (see
[goldlionren/gpu-unlock-4080s](https://github.com/Goldlionren/gpu-unlock-4080s);
its author flags FP8 variance and keeps FP8 out of that repo's own pass/fail
gate), and register-resident E4M3 probes read **603.1 TF/s** unlocked on the
modified 48 GB RTX 4090 (see [that evidence directory](docs/evidence/rtx4090-48g-modded/README.md))
and **165.45 → 323.95 TF/s (1.96×)** on a Windows RTX 4070 Ti SUPER (see
[A-XIANGQAQ/rtx4070tis-ad103-tensor-unlock](https://github.com/A-XIANGQAQ/rtx4070tis-ad103-tensor-unlock)).
The 4090 figure is 91% of its 660.6 TF/s full FP8 rate; NVIDIA rates a stock
RTX 4090 at 330.3 TF/s for FP8 with FP32 accumulate and 660.6 with FP16
accumulate.
So FP8 does move at the issue-rate level; a matched AD103 pair is 1.96×. At a
fixed power limit the application GEMM stays below that: an
unlocked RTX 4090 peaked at 346 W against 313 W stock and spent both MMA and
GEMM passes under SW Power Cap (see
[the 610.57.04 evidence](docs/evidence/rtx4090-610.57.04/README.md)).
This is one card; the unlock succeeded on two cold boots and two ordinary
warm reboots, the last from a persistent EFI default. Throughput was measured
on the first cold boot. See the [2705 canary report](docs/ada-2705-report.md)
and its [sanitized raw benchmark output](docs/evidence/ada2705/README.md).

The AD102 payload and its debug-booter analysis come from
**[TOTORONG/AD103_win_unlocker](https://huggingface.co/TOTORONG/AD103_win_unlocker)**.
This fork integrates that published payload into
**[Zagitta/gpu-unlock](https://github.com/Zagitta/gpu-unlock)**'s Linux module,
firmware generation and boot packaging. The payload is essential to the result.

## Experimental Windows contribution — Latence.app

A separate [MSI RTX 4070 Ti AD104 Windows UEFI reference port](windows/ad104-msi/README.md)
records one successful manual boot with NVIDIA 616.56 and matched cuBLAS FP16/FP32
**+80.1%**, BF16/FP32 **+76.4%** measurements. It is tied to one captured MSI Z490
profile; it does **not** add AD104 admission to the Linux module. See the
[report and limitations](docs/ad104-windows-latence-app.md). No firmware/Windows/ROM
binaries or automatic boot installer are distributed. Contribution by **Latence.app**;
original upstream credits and licences are retained.

## Supported targets

The module selects the AD102 firmware and payload automatically for RTX 4090
`10de:2684`. The original GeForce/CMP GA102/GA104 device list and GA102 payload
are retained, along with the newer GA103/GA106 device list. Upstream reported
RTX 3090 success; this branch does not revalidate every legacy board.
GA107 RTX 3050 6GB (`10de:2584`) uses the same GA102 Booter path and was
unlocked on one card ([2584 report](docs/ga107-2584-report.md)).

### Experimental Ada targets

Each ID below needs its own opt-in flag. Rows marked *exact* must also be
named by their exact PCI address in `gpu_unlock.targets=`, alone or in a
comma-separated list, and `targets=all` never selects them. All of them use the RTX 4090's pinned
AD102-family firmware and payload. Results come from one or a few cards per ID;
other boards, memory configurations and laptop models remain unverified.
`tools/print_boot_option.py` prints the exact option for any card listed here.

| PCI ID | Card | Die | Opt-in | Tested | Details |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `2685` | RTX 4090 D | AD102 | `rtx4090d_experimental` | eight cards in one host | [#7](https://github.com/JustAResearcher/gpu-unlock-ada/pull/7) |

Laptops differ in VBIOS ROM exposure, embedded-controller power rails and FLR
handling, so a result on one model does not carry over to another. Other Ada
IDs, professional RTX A-series and data-centre parts are not accepted. Shared
firmware across Ada chips does not establish support for untested cards.

The RTX 4090 path runs the signed firmware, checks the payload's completion marker and
required permissions, writes SS0 `0x88888888` and SS1 `0x8`, then performs FLR
before the unmodified NVIDIA driver binds. It requires the expected
effective speed-select readout before and after FLR. No patched NVIDIA driver or UEFI
application is needed. The payload uses instruction addresses derived from
published decrypted debug-booter analysis; the production booter is authenticated
and decrypted inside the GPU.

## Build and install

Clone the GPL-2.0-only source and build the packages locally so the pinned
NVIDIA firmware is downloaded and generated on your own machine:

```sh
git clone https://github.com/JustAResearcher/gpu-unlock-ada.git
cd gpu-unlock-ada
make install
```

`make install` detects the supported distribution family. Its explicit targets
are:

```sh
make install-arch   # makepkg -sif
make install-deb    # apt-get build-dep, dpkg-buildpackage, apt-get install
make install-rpm    # dnf builddep, rpmbuild, dnf install
```

`make arch`, `make deb` and `make rpm` build without installing. Packages are
built from the committed `HEAD`; Debian and RPM outputs go to `build/deb` and
`build/rpm`. Kernel headers and a working DKMS toolchain are required.

Builds fetch the pinned NVIDIA `610.43.03` source and binary inputs over HTTPS
and verify their SHA-256 hashes. `make inputs` prepares the cache;
`make firmware` generates assets from cached inputs; `make assets` does both.
The default cache is `$HOME/.cache/gpu-unlock` and can be overridden with
`CACHE=`, `INPUTS=` and `ASSETS=`. A clean-chroot Debian build needs
`GPU_UNLOCK_INPUTS` pointing to the input cache because `dpkg-buildpackage`
does not fetch inputs itself.

The source archive produced by `make dist`, the Debian source package and the
`.nosrc.rpm` contain no NVIDIA archives or generated firmware. See
[firmware/README.md](firmware/README.md) for the input and asset layout.
Prebuilt firmware packages are not distributed by this repository.

## Enable at boot

The package installs the module and firmware into the initramfs so the unlock
runs before NVIDIA binds the card. It remains inactive unless the kernel
command line opts in:

```text
gpu_unlock.targets=0000:03:00.0
gpu_unlock.targets=0000:03:00.0,0000:04:00.0
gpu_unlock.targets=all
gpu_unlock.targets=0000:01:00.0 gpu_unlock.ad103_experimental=1
```

These PCI addresses are examples. Use the full PCI names printed by `lspci -D`.
`all` selects every accepted unbound card, including legacy GA102/GA104 targets;
an explicit address is useful when selecting one RTX 4090. Do not mix `all` with
addresses. Every experimental Ada target requires its own flag from the
[experimental target table](#experimental-ada-targets), and the exact ones must
be named by their exact PCI address; `all` never selects them. Invalid entries
are logged and ignored.

The packages support these initramfs generators:

- **mkinitcpio:** `/etc/mkinitcpio.conf.d/zz-gpu-unlock.conf` puts `gpu_unlock`
  immediately before `nvidia` in `MODULES`, or last if NVIDIA is absent. Images
  are rebuilt on installation. A custom configuration selected with `-c` or a
  preset `_config` does not read drop-ins; add `gpu_unlock` before `nvidia` in
  that configuration's `MODULES` yourself.
- **initramfs-tools:**
  `/usr/share/initramfs-tools/modules.d/gpu-unlock.conf`.
- **dracut:** `/usr/lib/dracut/dracut.conf.d/gpu-unlock.conf`.

There is no `softdep nvidia pre:` rule because kmod uses only the first matching
soft dependency line, which can conflict with other packages.

**Power the machine off and start it again for the first attempt.** The module
needs a card whose firmware state is fresh before NVIDIA loads. A warm reboot
is not guaranteed to provide that state: it did on the tested
RTX 4070 Ti SUPER, where the pre-firmware WPR2 readback returned to zero and
the unlock succeeded again without an AC cut. Other boards may retain WPR2;
the module refuses to rerun the firmware sequence in that state. It also skips
cards that are already bound or powered down. If board firmware left bus
mastering enabled, the module clears it and verifies that it stayed cleared;
the later WPR2 check still rejects an already initialized card.
Loading the module manually after NVIDIA has bound the card cannot unlock it.

After validating a cold boot and a one-time warm reboot on the exact card, a
persistent bootloader entry can select the same early initramfs and exact
`gpu_unlock.*` options on every boot. A one-shot entry by itself does not
persist. Keep an unmodified stock entry available, and verify
`gpu_unlock: unlocked`, the rate readback and GPU health after each boot.
The tested canary uses a kernel-version-specific image; regenerate and
revalidate that image before removing its pinned kernel during an upgrade.

Avoid `nvidia-smi`, CUDA, NVML and `nvidia-modprobe` before a manual cold-card
attempt: they can load NVIDIA by name. Ordinary modprobe blacklist rules do not
block explicit named loads. The packaged initramfs flow avoids the need for
manual firmware staging and research parameters.

The original display-card handoff is retained: the firmware framebuffer is
removed just before FLR, and the display stays blank until `nvidia-drm` takes
over. Display handoff and multi-card operation were not part of the RTX 4090
validation.

## Check and disable

Inspect the kernel log after boot:

```sh
journalctl -k -b | grep gpu_unlock
lspci -nnk -s 0000:03:00.0  # replace the example address
```

A loaded module or successful `modprobe` return alone does not prove an unlock:
look for the selected card's `gpu_unlock: unlocked` message and the payload,
selector and post-FLR checks. The report describes independent register and
performance confirmation. The optional read-only sampler lives in
`diagnostics/peek`; the CUDA instruction benchmark is in `diagnostics/bench`.
Never load a second BAR0 sampler while `gpu_unlock` is performing its firmware
transaction.

If the module reports that firmware did not stop and its DMA buffers are being
kept, power off before trying again. The module intentionally retains buffers
that firmware may still use. Do not force-unload it in this state.

Remove `gpu_unlock.targets=` from the kernel command line to disable future
attempts. It can be removed for one boot in the bootloader editor. Removing the
packages removes the module and initramfs integration; power off to return to a
fresh hardware state.

## Development and credits

`make test` runs the host-side suite without accessing a GPU. Missing generated
firmware is reported as an explicit skip of the full transaction tests. After
`make assets`, use `make test-full` for a strict check that requires both the
pinned source and all generated assets. Override `ASSETS=` and `NVIDIA_SOURCE=`
for inputs built elsewhere. These tests mock firmware execution and device
behavior; they do not replace a hardware repeat.
See [testing and interpreting results](docs/testing.md) for the validation
levels, matched benchmark commands and recorded hardware evidence.

The kernel verifies each loaded asset against its pinned SHA-256 before claiming
the card or starting firmware DMA, including files staged into an initramfs.
The kernel's SHA-256 library (`CONFIG_CRYPTO_LIB_SHA256`) must be available.
`make -C kernel/gpu_unlock` builds against the running kernel's headers; use
`LLVM=1` when those headers support a Clang build.

The Linux module and packaging derive from
[Zagitta/gpu-unlock](https://github.com/Zagitta/gpu-unlock). The AD102 four-PLM
payload derives from
[TOTORONG/AD103_win_unlocker](https://huggingface.co/TOTORONG/AD103_win_unlocker),
including its published payload generator and debug-booter analysis. The GA102
V67 chain derives from
[WildFlash1st/cmp90hx-unlock](https://github.com/WildFlash1st/cmp90hx-unlock).
The earlier CMP unlock work, NVIDIA's published loader code, Nouveau and
[envytools](https://github.com/envytools/envytools) also underpin the loader and
investigation.

The kernel module, packaging and payload integration are GPL-2.0-only. NVIDIA
firmware remains under its own terms. See [firmware/NOTICE.md](firmware/NOTICE.md)
and [licenses/](licenses/) for provenance and preserved license notices.

items.description: HatchZip is a free, open-source archive extractor for Windows, macOS and Linux that extracts ZIP, 7z, RAR, tar and split archives in place, so it needs free space for the extracted files only. Desktop app and CLI.
items.readme:
HatchZip

Extract huge archives in place. The archive shrinks as your files hatch,
so you only need free space for the output, not for the output and the archive.

hatchzip.dev | Installation | Usage | Safety | How it works | Contributing

HatchZip is a free, open-source archive extractor for Windows, macOS and Linux, with a desktop app and a command line tool. It extracts ZIP, 7z, RAR, tar and split archives in place, for when there is not enough disk space to extract an archive next to itself, such as a large game download on a nearly full disk. Download it from [hatchzip.dev](https://hatchzip.dev). A 180 GB game download that unpacks to 200 GB needs 380 GB of disk with WinRAR, 7-Zip or `unzip`, because the archive and everything extracted from it have to exist at the same time. HatchZip needs a little over 200 GB. It extracts the archive from the end and cuts each finished part off the archive file as it goes, so the space the archive gives back is reused for the next files. It checks that the extraction will fit before it changes anything, keeps a safety margin of free space the whole way through, and can be stopped or crash at any moment and pick up where it left off. It reads ZIP, 7z, tar, `.tar.gz`, RAR volume sets and split archives. ### Get it > [!IMPORTANT] > HatchZip is only distributed from this repository's [releases](https://github.com/xevrion/hatchzip/releases) and its site, [hatchzip.dev](https://hatchzip.dev). Other sites using the name, such as hatchzip.com, are not affiliated with this project. No coding needed. **[Download for Windows](https://github.com/xevrion/hatchzip/releases/latest/download/HatchZip-x64-setup.exe)** (Windows 10 and 11), or for [macOS (Apple Silicon)](https://github.com/xevrion/hatchzip/releases/latest/download/HatchZip-aarch64.dmg), [macOS (Intel)](https://github.com/xevrion/hatchzip/releases/latest/download/HatchZip-x86_64.dmg) and [Linux](#installation). 1. Run the installer. Windows may show "Windows protected your PC" because HatchZip is not code-signed yet: choose **More info**, then **Run anyway**. 2. Right-click the archive, choose **HatchZip**, then **Extract here**. On Windows 11 the menu is under **Show more options**. 3. Or open HatchZip from the Start menu, open the archive, and choose **Extract**. HatchZip shows whether the files will fit before it changes anything. The archive is used up as the files come out, so when it finishes, only the extracted files are left. To keep the archive when there is room for both, choose **Extract here (keep archive)** in the right-click menu, or clear **Remove the archive during extraction** in the app. That is a normal extraction: the archive is not changed, and space is required for all extracted files. ## When there is not enough disk space to extract The same 200 MB of game data (21 files), packed by the real tools, extracted on a 220 MiB disk with about 50 MB free: | Archive | `unzip` / 7-Zip | HatchZip | |---|---|---| | ZIP, 180 MB | `unzip` ran out of space at file 6 of 21 | Finished, every file byte-identical | | 7z from 7-Zip 25.01, `-ms=20m` (10 solid blocks) | Needs 380 MB | Finished in 0.64 s, every file byte-identical | | 7z split into 5 volumes of 40 MB | Needs 380 MB | Finished; volumes deleted one at a time, peak 210 MB used | | tar from GNU tar, 200 MB | Needs 400 MB | Finished in 0.12 s, every file byte-identical | | 7z from 7-Zip with default settings (1 solid block) | Needs 380 MB | Refused before touching anything: one solid block can't be freed until all of it is out, so it needs 200 MB free | | | Result | |---|---| | ZIP extraction speed, same data | 0.25 to 0.35 s, against 1.48 to 1.50 s for `unzip` 6.00, including an fsync `unzip` skips | | Crash safety | Killed at both unsafe moments of a batch at many points of each format's run; every resume finished with identical output | | Works on | Any filesystem that can shrink a file: ext4, btrfs, XFS, NTFS, APFS, and also exFAT and FAT32 USB drives | Measured on Fedora 43, Intel Core i7-14700HX, SK Hynix NVMe SSD, warm page cache; the disk-space runs used a 220 MiB tmpfs to stand in for a full laptop disk, the speed runs ext4. Speed comes from decompressing files in parallel, so an archive holding one giant file extracts at the speed of a single core. The extra space HatchZip needs beyond the output is about the size of the largest single unit it can free at once: one file for ZIP and tar, one solid block for 7z. On filesystems that can punch holes (ext4, XFS, btrfs, tmpfs; NTFS and APFS not yet verified), a large file stored or deflated in a ZIP, or in a tar, frees its archive bytes every 256 MiB while it is extracted: a ZIP holding one 600 MiB stored file extracted on a 950 MiB tmpfs with 367 MB free, where it needed 629 MB before. `hatchzip check` computes the exact figure for any archive. ## Installation ### Desktop app Download from the [latest release](https://github.com/xevrion/hatchzip/releases/latest): | System | File | |---|---| | Windows 10 and 11 (x64) | [`HatchZip-x64-setup.exe`](https://github.com/xevrion/hatchzip/releases/latest/download/HatchZip-x64-setup.exe): installs per user, no admin rights, adds the right-click menu | | Windows 10 and 11 (x64), MSI | [`HatchZip-x64.msi`](https://github.com/xevrion/hatchzip/releases/latest/download/HatchZip-x64.msi): the same app and install as the setup, as a Windows Installer package for deployment tools and `msiexec /i HatchZip-x64.msi /qn`. Install one or the other | | macOS, Apple Silicon | [`HatchZip-aarch64.dmg`](https://github.com/xevrion/hatchzip/releases/latest/download/HatchZip-aarch64.dmg) | | macOS, Intel | [`HatchZip-x86_64.dmg`](https://github.com/xevrion/hatchzip/releases/latest/download/HatchZip-x86_64.dmg) | | Debian, Ubuntu | [`hatchzip_amd64.deb`](https://github.com/xevrion/hatchzip/releases/latest/download/hatchzip_amd64.deb) | | Fedora, openSUSE | [`hatchzip-x86_64.rpm`](https://github.com/xevrion/hatchzip/releases/latest/download/hatchzip-x86_64.rpm) | | Any Linux | [`HatchZip-x86_64.AppImage`](https://github.com/xevrion/hatchzip/releases/latest/download/HatchZip-x86_64.AppImage) | The installers also put the `hatchzip` command (and its short name `hz`) on your `PATH`. The Windows installers and the macOS apps are not code-signed yet: on Windows choose **More info**, then **Run anyway**; on macOS 15 and later, open the app once, then allow it under System Settings, Privacy & Security. ### Command line only Linux and macOS: ```sh curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xevrion/hatchzip/main/install.sh | sh ``` Windows, in PowerShell: ```powershell irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xevrion/hatchzip/main/install.ps1 | iex ``` Both download the build for your machine from the latest release, check it against its published SHA-256 checksum, and install `hatchzip` and `hz` for your user only, with the man page and shell completions. No root or administrator rights. Every release file from 0.1.3 on carries signed build provenance. To check that a download really was built from this repository by its release workflow, wherever you got it: ```sh gh attestation verify HatchZip-x64-setup.exe --repo xevrion/hatchzip ``` ### Package managers Homebrew and Scoop are live. winget is in review, and the AUR packages are coming soon; until they are listed as live here, a package under those names does not come from this project. | System | Command | Installs | |---|---|---| | Arch Linux (AUR) | `yay -S hatchzip-bin`, or `yay -S hatchzip` to build from source | App and CLI | | Windows (winget) | `winget install Xevrion.HatchZip` | App and CLI, same as the setup | | Windows (Scoop) | `scoop bucket add xevrion https://github.com/xevrion/scoop-bucket`, then `scoop install xevrion/hatchzip` | CLI | | macOS and Linux (Homebrew) | `brew install xevrion/tap/hatchzip` | CLI | | macOS (Homebrew) | `brew install --cask xevrion/tap/hatchzip` | App and CLI | ### With Cargo ```sh cargo install hatchzip ``` This builds the command line tool from [crates.io](https://crates.io/crates/hatchzip). The engine is a library too: [`hatchzip-core`](https://crates.io/crates/hatchzip-core). It reads every format but RAR; `cargo install hatchzip --features rar` adds RAR support, which compiles UnRAR's C++ source under its own [license](#license) and needs a C++ compiler. ### From source With [Rust](https://rustup.rs) (the version is pinned in `rust-toolchain.toml` and installed automatically): ```sh git clone https://github.com/xevrion/hatchzip.git cd hatchzip cargo build --release ``` The binaries are `target/release/hatchzip` and `target/release/hatchzip-gui` (`.exe` on Windows). Building the desktop app on Linux needs the fontconfig headers (`libfontconfig1-dev` or `fontconfig-devel`). `cargo build --release --features rar` adds RAR support, as in the release builds; it needs a C++ compiler. ### Shell completions and man page ```sh hatchzip completions bash > ~/.local/share/bash-completion/completions/hatchzip hatchzip completions zsh > "${fpath[1]}/_hatchzip" hatchzip completions fish > ~/.config/fish/completions/hatchzip.fish hatchzip completions powershell >> $PROFILE hatchzip man > ~/.local/share/man/man1/hatchzip.1 # then: man hatchzip ``` ## Usage ### See whether it fits ```sh hatchzip check game.zip ``` ``` game.zip 180.2 MB zip, 200.0 MB uncompressed in 22 entries available 50.5 MB standard extraction needs 200.0 MB required 29.9 MB (+5.0 MB reserved) available after 30.6 MB ``` `check` reads the archive's index and the disk's free space and changes nothing. "Standard extraction needs" is what extracting while keeping the archive requires; when that fits too, `check` says so. `hatchzip check game.zip --keep-archive` shows the plan for keeping it. ### Extract ```sh hatchzip extract game.zip # into ./game/ hatchzip extract game.zip -o D:\Games\Foo # somewhere else hatchzip x game.7z.001 # split archive; any part's name works ``` HatchZip prints the same space plan, asks for confirmation, then extracts. When the extraction is complete, the archive has been removed and the files are in the output folder. For a split archive, each volume is deleted as soon as everything in it is extracted. | Option | Effect | |---|---| | `-o, --output ` | Output folder. Defaults to a folder named after the archive, next to it. It may hold other files, but none where the archive's files go, unless `--replace` is given. | | `--keep-archive` | Keep the archive: a normal extraction that removes nothing. Space is required for all extracted files. No confirmation is asked. | | `--replace` | Replace files that already exist in the output folder. See [Extract over existing files](#extract-over-existing-files). | | `--keep-free ` | Free space HatchZip never uses, such as `500MB` or `10GB`. Default `2GB`, so the disk never fills to zero. | | `--verify-first` | Read the whole archive and check every file's checksum before deleting anything. Takes extra time, recommended for downloads you can't easily get again. | | `-y, --yes` | Skip the confirmation prompt. Required when not run from a terminal, unless `--keep-archive` is given. | | `-q, --quiet` | Print only errors and prompts. | ### Keep the archive ```sh hatchzip extract game.zip --keep-archive ``` When the disk has room for the archive and all its files, `--keep-archive` extracts like any other tool and leaves the archive byte for byte as it was, for when it is needed again. The space check, path and collision checks, checksums and password handling are the same as for an extraction in place. If keeping the archive does not fit, HatchZip says so, by how much, and what extracting in place would require instead. An interrupted run resumes like any other, and goes on keeping the archive even when resumed without `--keep-archive`. An extraction that started in place cannot switch to keeping the archive, since part of it is already removed. `hatchzip restore` on an archive being kept only discards the progress: the archive was never changed. ### Extract over existing files ```sh hatchzip extract patch.zip -o "D:\Games\Foo" --replace ``` HatchZip does not overwrite files. When a file the archive contains already exists in the output folder, extraction is refused before anything is changed, unless `--replace` is given, as for a game patch or a mod extracted over an installed game. In the desktop app, HatchZip asks instead, with the number of files. With `--replace`, before anything is extracted, every existing file or link at the path of a file in the archive is moved into a `.hatchzip-replaced` folder inside the output folder, keeping its relative path. The move is a rename on the same disk, so it needs no extra space and no data is copied; a link is moved, never followed. The replaced files are deleted when the extraction completes. The space plan is unchanged: the replaced files keep their space until the end. - An interrupted run resumes as usual, with or without `--replace`: the progress file records that files were moved aside. - `hatchzip restore` moves the replaced files back to where they were. An extraction in place is the exception: a file already extracted there is no longer in the archive, so the file it replaced stays in `.hatchzip-replaced`, and restore says how many did. With `--keep-archive`, every replaced file goes back. - A folder is never replaced: a folder where the archive has a file, or a file where it needs a folder, is refused as before. So is a link on the way to any path, and an archive that contains `.hatchzip-replaced` itself. ### Several archives ```sh hatchzip extract a.zip b.7z c.tar.gz ``` The archives are extracted one after another, each into its own folder, or all into the folder given with `-o`. The space for each one is checked just before it starts, so the space one archive frees is available to the next. The first archive that does not complete stops the run, and HatchZip lists which archives were extracted, which one stopped and whether its progress is saved, and which were not started; the exit status is that archive's. `check`, `test` and `list` also take several archives, go through all of them, and exit with the status of the first one that did not succeed. Naming every volume of a split archive, as a shell pattern like `game.7z.*` does, counts as that archive once. ### Stop and resume Press `Ctrl+C` and HatchZip finishes the files it is writing, saves its progress and exits. A second `Ctrl+C` quits immediately, which is also safe. To continue, run the same command again: ```sh hatchzip extract game.zip ``` The same applies after a crash, a power cut, or running out of space because something else filled the disk. Progress lives in two small files next to the archive, `game.zip.hatchzip` and `game.zip.hatchzip-tail`. **Do not delete them while an extraction is unfinished**: they hold the archive's index, which is no longer inside the archive itself. Anyone who supplies an archive could also supply progress files next to it, so HatchZip follows them only to the archive's own files, and only into the archive's default folder or one you chose for it. The folders you choose are noted in your user profile, outside the archive's folder, so a resume on the same computer needs no options. On another computer, name the folder again with `-o`; `restore` takes it too. ### Stop for good To give up on an unfinished extraction instead, restore the archive: ```sh hatchzip restore game.zip ``` What is left of the archive becomes a normal archive again, holding exactly the entries not yet extracted, which 7-Zip, WinRAR, `unzip` or `tar` open as usual. The files already extracted stay in the output folder. Restore only appends a new index, so it needs only the free space that index takes, and if it is interrupted, running it again finishes it. ### List and test ```sh hatchzip list game.7z # what's inside, with sizes hatchzip test game.7z # read every file and verify its checksum, writing nothing ``` Plain tar has no checksums for file contents, so `test` on a tar only proves every file can be read in full. ### Exit status | Code | Meaning | |---|---| | 0 | Success | | 1 | Failure. If extraction had started, progress is saved. | | 2 | Invalid command line | | 3 | Not enough free space. Nothing was changed. | | 4 | The archive is damaged. Nothing was deleted. | | 5 | The archive is password protected and no correct password was given. | | 130 | Paused with Ctrl+C. Run the same command to continue. | With several archives, the status is that of the first archive that did not succeed. ## Is HatchZip safe HatchZip destroys the archive as it extracts, so it is built around never losing a file that has not safely landed on disk. - **Nothing changes until the plan fits.** The space check runs before the first byte is touched, and it replays the whole extraction to find the moment that needs the most free space, not just the total. - **A file is written, flushed to the physical disk and renamed into place before the part of the archive holding it is cut off.** A crash at any point leaves either the file or its bytes in the archive, never neither. - **Damage stops the run where it is.** Every file's CRC-32 is checked as it is extracted. A damaged file is not written, and it stays in the archive along with everything before it. - **Hostile archives are refused before anything is deleted:** paths that escape the output folder, entries that overlap each other, entries that appear twice, and links where other entries need a folder. Setuid and setgid bits are never restored, and symlinks are created only after every regular file is written, so nothing can be written through one. Progress files found next to an archive are checked the same way: they may only name that archive's own volumes and links inside the output folder. - **A kept archive stays as it was.** With `--keep-archive`, the code that shrinks, frees or deletes archive bytes refuses to run for the whole extraction, and its progress file has a format older versions refuse, so none of them can resume it in place. - **A replaced file is never deleted early.** With `--replace`, existing files are moved aside, and the moves flushed to disk, before the first file is extracted, and they are deleted only when the extraction completes. The progress file records the move in a format older versions refuse, since they would not put the files back. What it cannot protect against: if the download itself is damaged, the files before the damaged spot are extracted and the archive is partly gone. Use `--verify-first` when the archive can't be downloaded again. On btrfs or APFS, space held by a snapshot that includes the archive is not freed until the snapshot is deleted. ### Antivirus warnings HatchZip does not connect to the network. It has no networking code and no networking library, and CI fails if an HTTP, TLS or socket crate enters the dependency tree ([deny.toml](deny.toml)). It collects nothing and sends nothing. The release files are not code-signed yet, and some antivirus engines that score files by machine learning or behaviour flag new, unsigned programs. On VirusTotal, the v0.1.3 Windows setup is flagged by 4 of 70 engines, all heuristic or machine-learning scores; Microsoft Defender reports it clean. What sandboxes list is what any installer does: it writes program files, adds the right-click menu and "Open with" entries, and runs Inno Setup's helper process. Code signing is planned. To check that a download is genuine, compare its SHA-256 with the `.sha256` file next to it, or verify that this repository's release workflow built it: ```sh gh attestation verify HatchZip-x64-setup.exe --repo xevrion/hatchzip ``` [Verify your download](https://hatchzip.dev/verify.html) has the commands for every system and the checksum of every release file, each with its VirusTotal report. Or build it yourself: `cargo install hatchzip`. ## Supported formats | Format | Status | Freed in steps of | |---|---|---| | ZIP, ZIP64, self-extracting `.exe` ZIPs | Supported. Tested: Stored, Deflate, Deflate64, bzip2, LZMA, PPMd, XZ and Zstandard, including archives made by 7-Zip itself, and entries past the 4 GiB mark. | One file | | 7z, solid and non-solid | Supported. Tested with archives made by 7-Zip 25.01: LZMA2 (its default), LZMA, BCJ with LZMA2, bzip2, Deflate and PPMd; Zstandard with an archive made by py7zr, since 7-Zip has no Zstandard coder for the 7z format. | One solid block | | tar (uncompressed) | Supported, including long names, symlinks and hard links | One file | | `.tar.gz`, `.tgz` | Supported, including multi-member gzip (`bgzip`, `pigz -i`) and split `.tar.gz.001` sets. Extracted from the front, freeing the compressed bytes behind the decoder where the filesystem can punch holes; every gzip CRC-32 and length is checked before anything is touched. Tested with archives from GNU tar with gzip, and pigz. Elsewhere (FAT32, exFAT) it still extracts and resumes, but needs room for the archive and every file at once, and `check` says so. | 256 MiB of output | | Split archives (`.001`, `.002`, ...) of ZIP or 7z, as 7-Zip makes them | Supported | One file or block; each volume is deleted once emptied | | Password-protected ZIP (ZipCrypto and AES) and 7z (AES, including encrypted file lists) | Supported. HatchZip asks for the password, or takes `--password` or `HATCHZIP_PASSWORD`, and proves it on one file before anything is deleted. It is never saved, so a resumed run asks again. | Same as unencrypted | | `.tar.zst`, `.tar.xz` | Refused before extraction, planned; see [the format notes](docs/formats.md#tarzst-and-tarxz). | | | One huge solid 7z block | Works, but needs free space for the whole block, as the table above shows. Freeing space inside a block is the same planned technique. | | | RAR, RAR 5 and RAR 4, single files and volume sets (`.part1.rar`, `.part2.rar`, ... or `.rar`, `.r00`, ...) | Supported in the release builds, decoded by UnRAR (see [License](#license)); builds without the `rar` feature, such as `cargo install hatchzip`, refuse RAR before anything is touched. Password-protected files work as for ZIP: a RAR 5 password is proven by its check value, a RAR 4 one by decoding the smallest encrypted file, which for a large file can take a while. Archives with encrypted file names ("Encrypt file names", `rar -hp`) need the password even to be listed, and are freed file by file like any other. A large stored file is freed while it is written, as in tar. Refused before anything is touched: links, dictionaries over 4 GB, and sets with a volume missing or a stray one after the last. `restore` works, except for archives with encrypted file names, since it takes no password; such an extraction can only be completed. Tested with archives made by RAR 6.24 (RAR 5 and RAR 4) and archives written by the test suite; sets made by WinRAR 7.23 were tested on Windows when RAR support was first written. | One file; a volume once every file that reaches into it is out | | Solid RAR | Extracted only while the archive is kept (`--keep-archive`): a solid archive decodes front to back in one pass and UnRAR can't save its state, so it can't be freed as it goes or resumed mid-way. In place, it is refused before anything is touched. | | | Native split ZIP (`.z01`) | Planned | | ## How it works ZIP, 7z and tar all store their contents as a sequence of independent pieces: files for ZIP and tar, solid blocks for 7z. ZIP and 7z keep their index at the very end. HatchZip saves that index to a side file, then extracts pieces starting from the last one in the archive. After each batch it truncates the archive to where that batch began, which every operating system and filesystem supports; for a split archive, that means deleting whole volumes and shortening one. RAR stores files one after another like tar, so it is freed file by file too, and a volume is deleted once every file reaching into it is out. A `.tar.gz` is one compressed stream that can only be decoded from the front, so HatchZip extracts it front to back and punches holes in the compressed bytes it has used, at resume points it can restart from after a crash. The full design, including the exact order of writes that makes a crash safe, is in [How it works](docs/how-it-works.md). ## How it is built HatchZip is written with the help of AI coding assistants, and [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) is the rulebook they work under. It is the strict part of the project: the tool deletes its own input, so a change only lands with proof. - **More than 130 tests run on Linux, macOS and Windows** for every change, in CI on real machines of each kind. - **Crash tests kill the process at every step** where it writes a file, saves its progress or cuts the archive, then resume and compare every extracted file byte for byte. - **Freeing space is checked, not assumed.** CI fails if ext4, APFS or NTFS do not really give the space back. - **Damaged and hostile archives are part of the suite:** paths that escape the folder, overlapping entries, bad CRCs, truncated downloads, wrong passwords. - **Every number in this README was measured** on real hardware, and the conditions are written next to it. Pull requests and bug reports from people are held to the same rules, and are very welcome. ## Star history ## License HatchZip is licensed under either of [Apache License, Version 2.0](LICENSE-APACHE) or [MIT license](LICENSE-MIT), at your option. RAR archives are decoded by the UnRAR source code, which is freeware under its own [license](LICENSE-UNRAR): free to use for extracting RAR archives, but not to build a RAR compatible archiver. It is compiled in only with the `rar` cargo feature, which is off by default, so `cargo install hatchzip`, the crates on crates.io and distribution builds are open source throughout and need no C++ compiler. The release builds on the [releases page](https://github.com/xevrion/hatchzip/releases) have it on, and every release download includes `LICENSE-UNRAR`. ## Contributing Bug reports, especially from filesystems and operating systems not covered by CI, are welcome. Read [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) first. Unless you explicitly state otherwise, any contribution intentionally submitted for inclusion in HatchZip by you, as defined in the Apache-2.0 license, shall be dual licensed as above, without any additional terms or conditions.

items.readme:
# 3D Model Anything

[![Watch the video: 3D Model Anything](docs/images/thumb-1.png)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JGQCcCzuS88)

Capture a room on an iPhone, then use its geometry and photographs to build an editable Three.js scene with an AI coding agent.

[Open the office viewer](https://wesbos.github.io/3d-model-anything/) · [App support](https://wesbos.github.io/3d-model-anything/support.html)

This repository includes the **3D Model Anything iPhone app**, a **Three.js viewer**, the **scan-to-threejs agent skill**, and **Wes’s detailed office demo**.

The app records the evidence. The skill guides an agent through measurement, modeling and matched-camera visual comparisons. This is an iterative reconstruction workflow, not a one-click scan-to-perfect-model converter. The current workflow focuses on rooms and interiors.

## Run the viewer

Use Node.js 22.12+ (or a newer supported release).

```sh
npm ci
npm run dev
```

Open http://localhost:5188. Explore the office in dollhouse, walking, overhead, wireframe and knolling views. The playground is at `/play.html?room=office-v4&mode=fpv`.

```sh
npm run build
npm run preview
```

The demo includes the reconstructed office and selected textures. Original scans and photo collections are not distributed; Scan and Overlay are disabled for this example. Those modes remain available for your own rooms with reference assets.

## Capture your own space

See [the iPhone app](apps/house-capture/README.md) for building with Xcode, device requirements, scanning and sharing. Scanning needs a LiDAR-equipped iPhone or iPad. Non-LiDAR devices can import and review scans.

The app is source-available here; an App Store release is a separate distribution step. Do not assume an App Store download is available yet.

Export a room or session through the system share sheet and extract it into an ignored `data/captures-in/<room>/` directory. Exports keep the existing `house-capture/5` contract; changing the app name does not change the files.

## Use the skill

The skill lives at `.agents/skills/scan-to-threejs/SKILL.md`. Open this repository in an agent that supports local skills and ask it to use **scan-to-threejs** with your extracted export. You can also copy that skill directory into your agent's skill directory; the companion viewer/runtime in this repo is still needed for its capture workflow.

Example request:

> Use scan-to-threejs to rebuild the room in data/captures-in/my-room. Inspect the measurements and photos, create an editable scene, and compare rendered views with the original photographs.

Start with [the format guide](.agents/skills/scan-to-threejs/references/house-capture.md) and [project layout](.agents/skills/scan-to-threejs/references/project-layout.md). Helpers need Python 3; photo comparisons need Pillow, and optional depth reconstruction needs NumPy, Open3D and Pillow. Capture scripts use the `agent-browser` CLI.

A new room goes in `demos/<id>/` and is registered in `demos/index.ts`. The office example retains its earlier reconstruction layers (`office-v2`, `office-latest`, `office-v4`) to preserve the final geometry.

## Privacy and licensing

Only the office example is distributed. No other rooms, connected-house layout, original scan bundles, or development Git history are included. Keep your captures private; inspect assets before publishing your own demo.

Reusable source code and the skill are MIT licensed. The supplied office images/textures have separate [asset terms](ASSETS-LICENSE.md). Third-party marks, artwork and depicted products are not licensed by the code license.

See [release status](docs/release-status.md) for validation and iPhone distribution steps.

items.readme:
php2shell

CVE-2026-109618 & CVE-2026-109619 — PHP Pre-Auth RCE Exploit & Detection Toolkit

Exploits · Detection · Lab · Writeup

--- Five independent RCE chains exploiting PHP's `session.upload_progress` and the Zend engine's OOM bailout. **14 years of vulnerable code** — PHP 5.4.0 (2012) through 8.5.11. Pre-auth. No application vulnerability required for some chains. Impacts **78% of all websites** — including WordPress (43%), Joomla, Drupal, Laravel, Magento, and every default PHP installation. **Author:** [Qi Deng](https://github.com/ikow)  |  **Writeup:** [Substack](https://qideng.substack.com/p/php2shell-dissecting-phps-critical)  |  **Date:** 2026-10-21 ## CVE Details | CVE | GHSA | CVSS | Description | |-----|------|------|-------------| | CVE-2026-109618 | [GHSA-w8hw-w9fx-j79w](https://github.com/php/php-src/security/advisories/GHSA-w8hw-w9fx-j79w) | 9.2 | OOM → `longjmp()` leaves Zend engine state invalid → RCE | | CVE-2026-109619 | [GHSA-6wmf-4rv5-p3rp](https://github.com/php/php-src/security/advisories/GHSA-6wmf-4rv5-p3rp) | 9.2 | Stale global state across FPM worker requests → UAF → RCE | **Patch:** [Commit 3584a98](https://github.com/php/php-src/commit/3584a98bda) — 300 files changed across the Zend engine. ## Attack Chains | Chain | Vector | Pre-auth | Conditions | SAPI | |-------|--------|:--------:|------------|------| | **A** | Session injection + LFI | Yes | App has any LFI sink | All | | **B** | var_destroy UAF → handler overwrite | No | App calls `unserialize()` | All | | **C** | Handler mismatch → `__destruct` | Yes | Two dirs with different serialize_handler | FPM | | **D** | OOM corruption → stale `EG()` | Yes | **None** — any endpoint | mod_php | | **E** | FPM session OOM → stale `BG()` | Yes | Producer: any `session_start()` endpoint; Consumer: **any** endpoint | FPM | Chain D is the most critical: **zero-dependency pre-auth RCE** against any Apache mod_php installation. Chain E is nearly as broad on FPM: the producer needs any endpoint that calls `session_start()` (near-universal — WordPress, Laravel, Joomla, Drupal all do), and the **consumer can be any PHP endpoint** — the `rfc1867` upload_progress handler runs during SAPI startup before application code. Verified: `nosession.php` (no `session_start()` in code) triggers 502 crash when consuming stale `BG(unserialize)` state. ## Exploits Three RCE exploits (Chains A, B, C) are included in [`exploit/`](exploit/): | File | Chain | What It Does | |------|-------|-------------| | `chain_a_session_lfi.py` | A | Injects PHP code via upload filename → LFI includes session file → RCE | | `chain_b_uaf_rce.php` | B | var_destroy UAF → discovers `zif_system` via EG() → overwrites `var_dump` handler via `/proc/self/mem` → RCE | | `chain_c_mismatch_rce.py` | C | Pollutes FPM worker `PS(serializer)` → injects serialized object via filename → `__destruct` fires on decode failure → RCE | Chains D and E exploits are available to [paid subscribers](https://qideng.substack.com/p/php2shell-dissecting-phps-critical). ```bash # Chain A: Session injection + LFI → RCE python3 exploit/chain_a_session_lfi.py --host TARGET --port 80 --command 'id' # Chain B: var_destroy UAF → RCE (run on target or via uploaded webshell) php exploit/chain_b_uaf_rce.php # Chain C: Handler mismatch → __destruct → RCE python3 exploit/chain_c_mismatch_rce.py --host TARGET --port 80 --command 'id' ``` ## Detection Rules Pre-built IDS / WAF / SIEM rules in [`detection/`](detection/): | File | Format | Signatures | |------|--------|-----------| | `php2shell.rules` | Suricata / Snort | 13 rules — request, response, and recon | | `php2shell.yaml` | Sigma | 5 rules — web logs, process creation, file events | | `modsecurity.conf` | ModSecurity v2/v3 | 7 rules — drop-in for Apache/Nginx | | `php2shell.lua` | OpenResty Lua | Lightweight reverse proxy module | **Fastest mitigation:** block `PHP_SESSION_UPLOAD_PROGRESS` in multipart POST bodies. Near-zero legitimate use, covers the primary attack vector for both CVEs. ## Quick Start ```bash git clone https://github.com/ikow/php2shell-poc.git && cd php2shell-poc # Start the lab (PHP-FPM + nginx + Apache mod_php) cd lab && docker compose up -d # Verify each chain python3 ../poc/verify_session_injection.py --target http://127.0.0.1:18080 python3 ../poc/verify_handler_mismatch.py --target http://127.0.0.1:18080 python3 ../poc/verify_oom_trigger.py --host 127.0.0.1 --port 18081 python3 ../poc/verify_fpm_stale_state.py --target http://127.0.0.1:18080 # Run an exploit python3 ../exploit/chain_a_session_lfi.py --host 127.0.0.1 --port 18080 --command 'id' ``` ## Repository Structure ``` php2shell-poc/ ├── exploit/ │ ├── chain_a_session_lfi.py # RCE: session injection + LFI │ ├── chain_b_uaf_rce.php # RCE: var_destroy UAF → handler overwrite │ └── chain_c_mismatch_rce.py # RCE: handler mismatch → __destruct ├── detection/ │ ├── php2shell.rules # Suricata / Snort IDS rules │ ├── php2shell.yaml # Sigma SIEM detection rules │ ├── modsecurity.conf # ModSecurity WAF rules │ └── php2shell.lua # OpenResty / Nginx Lua WAF module ├── poc/ │ ├── verify_session_injection.py # Verify Chain A │ ├── verify_uaf_asan.php # Verify Chain B (ASAN) │ ├── verify_handler_mismatch.py # Verify Chain C │ ├── verify_oom_trigger.py # Verify Chain D │ └── verify_fpm_stale_state.py # Verify Chain E ├── lab/ │ ├── docker-compose.yml # PHP-FPM + nginx + Apache mod_php │ ├── setup.sh # One-click lab setup │ └── php.ini / php-apache.ini # Vulnerable PHP configs └── docs/ ├── ANALYSIS.md # Full technical analysis └── substack_article.md # Writeup source ``` ## Mitigation ```ini ; Immediate — reduces attack surface session.upload_progress.enabled = Off session.use_only_cookies = On ``` > **The only complete fix is patching PHP** to 8.2.35 / 8.3.36 / 8.4.27 / 8.5.12+. The OOM corruption (Chain D) is in the Zend engine core — no INI setting fixes it. ## Downstream Impact Wiz has demonstrated pre-auth RCE on stock container images: | Platform | Vulnerable | Notes | |----------|:----------:|-------| | WordPress | Yes | Core doesn't use PHP sessions, but WooCommerce and many plugins do | | Joomla | Yes | Uses native PHP sessions by default | | Drupal | Yes | Uses native PHP sessions by default | | Magento | Yes | Vulnerable even in maintenance mode | | Laravel | Yes | `PendingBroadcast` is a known `__destruct` gadget | ## References - [PHP Security Advisory](https://www.php.net/archive/2026.php) - [GHSA-w8hw-w9fx-j79w](https://github.com/php/php-src/security/advisories/GHSA-w8hw-w9fx-j79w) — CVE-2026-109618 - [GHSA-6wmf-4rv5-p3rp](https://github.com/php/php-src/security/advisories/GHSA-6wmf-4rv5-p3rp) — CVE-2026-109619 - [Patch commit 3584a98](https://github.com/php/php-src/commit/3584a98bda) — 300 files, Zend engine + extensions - [Cloudflare WAF coverage](https://blog.cloudflare.com/php-vulnerabilities-waf-protection/) - [Sansec analysis](https://sansec.io/research/php2shell) — PHPSESSID heap leak discovery - [Wiz downstream impact](https://www.wiz.io/blog/php2shell-php-rce) - [Corelight detection](https://github.com/corelight/php2shell-detect) — Zeek + Suricata community rules ## Disclaimer This repository is for **authorized security testing and educational purposes only**. Exploit code for Chains D and E (zero-dependency RCE) is available to [paid subscribers](https://qideng.substack.com/p/php2shell-dissecting-phps-critical) of the writeup. ## License MIT ---

Keywords: php2shell, CVE-2026-109618, CVE-2026-109619, PHP RCE, PHP exploit, session.upload_progress, pre-auth RCE, PHP vulnerability, PHP session injection, PHP deserialization, PHP OOM, PHP memory corruption, use-after-free, GHSA-w8hw-w9fx-j79w, GHSA-6wmf-4rv5-p3rp, WordPress RCE, Joomla RCE, Drupal RCE, PHP security, WAF rules, Suricata rules, ModSecurity rules, IDS signatures, PHP 8.2.35, PHP 8.4.27, session upload progress, PHP session fixation, rfc1867, longjmp, zend_bailout, Snort rules, Sigma rules, detection rules, PHP patch, PHP critical vulnerability

items.readme:
# The Day Trader skill

11 Claude skills for day trading: scan thousands of charts, track breaking news, time every entry and exit, and replay every outcome before you risk a dollar.

Free, MIT, no signup, no API key. The tools are plain Python that read free
public data: Yahoo Finance charts, Nasdaq Trader's symbol lists, SEC EDGAR
and the House Clerk.

One scans thousands of charts for setups. Another tracks breaking news on
every stock you watch. One watches a setup bar by bar and tells you the moment
to get in, and another sets your stop and your target before you do. And the
craziest one is the Time Machine: before you risk a dollar, it replays the
rest of the session 10,000 times from the stock's own recent bars, plus every
past day the same setup fired, and tells you the honest odds.

And no trade goes through until you say yes. Nothing in this pack can place
an order on its own. Paper trading is the default.

> **Looking for the original Trader skill?** Copy an investor's 13F, the
> stock screener, tax lots and rebalancing live in
> [github.com/Jakeschincariol/trader-skill](https://github.com/Jakeschincariol/trader-skill).
> This repo is its day-trading sequel: the Trader skill v2.

## Install

Paste this into Claude:

```
https://github.com/Jakeschincariol/day-trader-skill

install skill
```

Or as a plugin, in Claude Code:

```
/plugin marketplace add Jakeschincariol/day-trader-skill
/plugin install day-trader-skill@day-trader-skill
```

Claude Code namespaces plugin skills, so installed as a plugin they show up as
`/day-trader-skill:trader-scanner` and so on. Copy the folders instead if you want
plain `/trader-scanner`:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/Jakeschincariol/day-trader-skill.git
cp -r day-trader-skill/trader-* ~/.claude/skills/
```

Project-local instead of global: copy the same folders into your repo's
`.claude/skills/`. No Claude Code at all? Paste any single `SKILL.md` at the
top of a chat and it runs as a mode. You lose the Python tools, but the method
works.

The tools need Python 3.8 or newer. Nothing to pip install. The SEC tools
(news filings, the analyst) ask you to identify yourself: put your name and
email in `trader/config.json` (`"sec_user_agent": "Your Name you@example.com"`)
or in the `SEC_USER_AGENT` environment variable.

## The eleven

| command | job | what it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `/trader-scanner` | Chart Scanner | Scans thousands of charts for setups: opening-range breakouts, flags, oversold bounces. |
| `/trader-news` | News Monitor | Tracks breaking news on every stock you watch and flags what moves it. |
| `/trader-entry` | Entry Timer | Watches a setup bar by bar and tells you the moment to get in. |
| `/trader-exit` | Exit Planner | Sets your stop and your target before you enter, so you know when to get out. |
| `/trader-timemachine` | Time Machine | Replays every possible outcome of a trade before you risk a dollar: 10,000 simulated sessions plus every past time the setup fired. |
| `/trader-risk` | Risk Manager | Checks every trade against your limits and stops anything over them. |
| `/trader-budget` | Budget Manager | Sizes every position to your budget and your max loss per trade. |
| `/trader-broker` | Order Executor | Sends approved orders to your broker, paper trading by default, never without your yes. |
| `/trader-alerts` | Price Alerts | Rings when a price, a stop or the opening bell hits. |
| `/trader-analyst` | Earnings Analyst | Reads earnings reports and sums up what changed. |
| `/trader-pelosi` | Pelosi Tracker | Reads Congress's stock-trade disclosures the minute they are filed. |

## How to use it

Everything lands in a `trader/` folder in your project, and each skill reads
what the last one wrote:

```
scanner -> news -> entry -> exit -> timemachine -> budget -> risk -> broker   (one trade)
alerts: stop, target, flat by the close                                       (while it is open)
news / analyst / pelosi                                                        (on a schedule)
```

An example, the trade in the reel: Tesla, Monday October 19 2026, real data.

1. **`/trader-scanner`** at 10:15 AM ET: of the 231 charts in the reel's
   scan, 42 had closed above their 15-minute opening range. TSLA is one: range 354.47 to 362.18,
   the 10:10 candle closed at 364.18, 0.55 % over the top.
2. **`/trader-news`**: the morning's TSLA headlines, in New York time
   ("Tesla-SpaceX Merger Mania Strikes Wall Street Ahead of Earnings", 8:04,
   tagged earnings and deal). Tesla reports this week: a day trade is out
   before the close, so it is not exposed to the report.
3. **`/trader-entry`** watched TSLA bar by bar. At 10:12 it said waiting (the
   10:10 bar was still forming). At 10:15 it said triggered: the first
   5-minute close above the range, 364.18.
4. **`/trader-exit`** set the plan before the entry: stop at the range's
   midpoint, 358.32, so 5.86 a share at risk; target one times that risk,
   370.04; flat by 3:55 PM either way.
5. **`/trader-timemachine`** replayed the rest of the day 10,000 times, each
   5-minute candle drawn from TSLA's own candles at that time of day over the
   previous 59 sessions (seed 19, so anyone can repeat it): target first
   29.4 %, stop first 25.5 %, still open at the close 45.1 %. It also re-ran
   the same rule on those 59 real sessions: it fired 33 times, 13 hit the
   target, 15 the stop, 5 neither. Its verdict: close to a coin flip. That is
   the point of looking before you risk a dollar.
6. **`/trader-budget`** with a $5,000 account and a $50 max loss per trade:
   50 / 5.86 = 8 shares ($2,913.44). If the stop fills at 358.32, the loss is
   $46.88. It writes one bracket order: buy 8 TSLA, stop-loss 358.32,
   take-profit 370.04.
7. **`/trader-risk`** checks it against your limits: the max loss, the daily
   loss limit, trades per day, reward to risk, the entry window, position
   size and cash. PASS or BLOCK, with the reason.
8. **`/trader-broker`** shows you the ticket in plain words. You type yes for
   that exact order. Claude calls your brokerage connector (Alpaca's MCP
   server, paper account by default), and Claude's own "Allow once / Deny"
   card asks you one more time.
9. **`/trader-alerts`** rings on the stop, the target and at 3:55 PM to
   flatten whatever is still open.

## The tools

All standard-library Python. The data tools read public endpoints and are
polite about it.

```bash
python3 trader-scanner/scan.py universe                                # ~5,900 US stocks, Nasdaq Trader
python3 trader-scanner/scan.py daily                                   # pre-market setups, whole universe
python3 trader-scanner/scan.py orb --at 10:15                          # opening-range breakouts so far
python3 trader-news/news.py --tickers TSLA --hours 12                  # headlines, 8-Ks, today's move
python3 trader-entry/entry.py check TSLA --setup orb                   # waiting / triggered / expired
python3 trader-entry/entry.py watch TSLA --every 30                    # bar by bar until it triggers
python3 trader-exit/exit.py plan --stop or-mid --target 1R --write     # -> trader/plan.json
python3 trader-timemachine/timemachine.py run --write                  # 10,000 replays + the history
python3 trader-budget/size.py --write                                  # -> trader/orders.json
python3 trader-risk/check.py                                           # PASS / BLOCK per order
python3 trader-broker/ticket.py show                                   # the tickets, READY or not
python3 trader-alerts/alerts.py add --from-plan                        # stop, target, flat by close
python3 trader-alerts/alerts.py check                                  # rings what hit, once
python3 trader-analyst/facts.py TSLA                                   # quarters, growth, EPS
python3 trader-pelosi/ptr.py index --member pelosi                     # her PTRs this year
```

```bash
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v
```

The tests run offline, on fixtures cut from real data: TSLA's 5-minute bars
for the 60 days to October 19 2026, the 10:15 AM opening-range scan, Yahoo's
TSLA headlines that morning, the House Clerk's 2026 index, real PTR text and
real XBRL facts. They reproduce every number in the example above.

## Fine print

**Not financial advice.** This is software that reads public data and does
arithmetic. It does not know your situation and it cannot see the future.
Most people who day trade lose money. You can lose money. Decide for
yourself, and talk to a licensed professional if you need advice.

**No trade goes through until you say yes.** Only `/trader-broker` can lead to
an order, and only after `/trader-risk` passes that exact order and you type
yes for it in the chat. Set your brokerage tool to "Needs approval" in Claude
(Customize, Connectors, tool permissions), never "Always allow", so Claude's
own "Allow once / Deny" card is a second check. No options, margin, short
selling or leverage unless you turn them on.

**Paper first.** `"paper": true` is the default in `config.example.json`, and
Alpaca's MCP server defaults to its paper account. Keys live in environment
variables, never in the chat.

**The Time Machine is a simulation, not a prediction.** It is built from the
stock's own last 60 days of 5-minute bars. The future can do things those 60
days never did: an earnings report, a halt, a headline. Treat its odds as a
reality check, never as a promise.

**A stop is a plan, not a guarantee.** In a fast market or across a gap, a
stop order can fill well past its price. The max loss shown is the loss at
the stop price.

**The data is free and unofficial.** Yahoo Finance's chart endpoint is not an
official API: it can lag, change or rate-limit you. The scanner and the entry
timer read 1-minute or 5-minute bars, not every tick. Check anything that
matters against your broker before you act on it.

**Day-trading rules.** FINRA removed the $25,000 pattern-day-trader minimum
on June 4, 2026 (Regulatory Notice 26-10), and brokers may phase the change
in until October 20, 2027, so yours may still apply the old rule. If it does,
set `"pdt_guard": true` and `/trader-risk` counts your day trades.

**Congress's trades are public, not inside information.** Members must disclose
trades over $1,000 within 45 days (the STOCK Act). The Pelosi skill reads those
public filings the minute they post.

**Taxes.** Day-trading gains are short-term gains, and frequent trading makes
wash sales likely. Nothing here is tax advice.
